lines.japanese: 「あいよ、ストロベリーヨーグルト一丁お待ち！」
lines.english: “One strawberry yogurt, ready and waiting!”

lines.japanese: しばらくして、まるで下町の魚屋みたいなパル姐さんの声があがった。
lines.english: After a while, Paru's voice rose in the cadence of a fishmonger from old downtown.

lines.japanese: 「あー、はーい」
lines.english: “Oh, yes.”

lines.japanese: あとに続く間延びした返事。なんだ、あの小娘、クレープ待ちだったのか。
lines.english: The same drawn-out reply followed. Oh. The girl had only been waiting for her crêpe.

lines.japanese: 「えー、おいくらですかー」
lines.english: “Um, how much do I owe you?”

lines.japanese: 「いらないよ」
lines.english: “Nothing.”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 始まった。パルさんは見た目通りの姐御肌で、若いやつとか困ってるやつには甘いんだ。
lines.english: Here we go. Paru was every inch the big-hearted woman she looked, with a weakness for the young and the troubled.

lines.japanese: 「きょうの分はおごりさ。あたし、あんたっこと気に入っちまったい。おまえさんとの縁にゃあ５００円分の価値があらァな」
lines.english: “This one is on me. I’ve taken a liking to you. Meeting you is worth five hundred yen to me.”

lines.japanese: 「い、いえー！　だめですそんな、払います！」
lines.english: “N-no! You can't do that. I'll pay!”

lines.japanese: 「いいんだって。そんかし、今後あんたが柳木原でクレープ食いたくなったときァ、ぜひうちを贔屓にしておくれ」
lines.english: “I said it's fine. In exchange, next time you want a crêpe in Yanagihara, make sure you come back to my shop.”

lines.japanese: 「いえー、でもー……」
lines.english: “No, but...”

lines.japanese: 「いいから、とっととそのガマ口ひっこめな。おごられ下手はイイ女になれないよ」
lines.english: “Enough. Put that coin purse away. A girl who can't accept a treat will never grow into a fine woman.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんですか？」
lines.english: “Is that true?”

lines.japanese: 客がカウンターに身を乗りだしたせいで、車体が大きく片側に傾いた。こんな童顔のチビっ子にも将来の夢はあったようだ。
lines.english: The customer leaned over the counter so far the whole van listed sharply to one side. Apparently even this baby-faced runt cherished dreams for her future.

lines.japanese: 「はー、そーかー、それではお言葉に甘えさせていただきますねー明日のために」
lines.english: “Ahh, I see. Then I'll gratefully accept—for the sake of tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: 「おうよ。自転車見つかるよう頑張んな」
lines.english: “That's the spirit. Do your best to find your bicycle.”

lines.japanese: イキでイナセな姐御の笑顔。パルさんは人情と義侠心を重んじる街の出身だった。
lines.english: The smile of a gallant, streetwise woman. Paru was from the sort of neighborhood that still valued human feeling and chivalrous duty.

lines.japanese: 凍える夜に出会ったちょっといい話。油膜まで消えてフロントガラスもぴかぴかだ。めでたしめでたし。
lines.english: A little heartwarming story for a freezing night. The oily film was gone, the windshield gleamed, and everyone lived happily ever after.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、そーゆーことで」
lines.english: “Right. With that settled.”

lines.japanese: 「待ちな」
lines.english: “Hold it.”

lines.japanese: バックドアに回りこんでバケツその他を返したら、いきなりクレープ屋に手首を捕まれてしまった。
lines.english: When I went around to the rear doors to return the bucket and supplies, the crêpe seller suddenly seized my wrist.

lines.japanese: 俺はじろりとやつを睨む。
lines.english: I glared at her.

lines.japanese: 「なに」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「どこ行くんだい、坊主」
lines.english: “Where are you going, kid?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、だから最初から言ってんじゃん。仕事探しに行くんだよ」
lines.english: “I’ve been telling you from the start. I’m going to look for work.”

lines.japanese: 「良かったな。見つかったじゃないか」
lines.english: “Good news. You found it.”

lines.japanese: 手首を掴む握力が強くなった。ぐいと引きよせられ、耳元に鋭い声が走る。
lines.english: Her grip tightened around my wrist. She yanked me close and hissed into my ear.

lines.japanese: 「この子のチャリ探し、引きうけなって成田工務店」
lines.english: “Take the job. Find this girl's bicycle, Narita Construction.”

lines.japanese: 「はァァ？」
lines.english: “What!?”

lines.japanese: 思わず変な声が出た。学生服の小娘が、クレープにパクついたままの首を曲げて俺たちを見る。とりあえず無視した。
lines.english: A strange noise escaped me. The uniformed girl craned around to look at us without stopping mid-bite. I ignored her for the moment.

lines.japanese: 「だから、しつけーってパルクレープ」
lines.english: “I told you to drop it, Paru Crêpes.”

lines.japanese: 「あんな？　さっきも言ったろ？　俺だって生活あんだよ、慈善事業じゃねンだよ。じゃあよ、その途方もない年月を費やしそうなお仕事のご依頼料、あのガキもしくはあんたが払ってくれんの」
lines.english: “Listen. I said this already, didn't I? I have to make a living. This isn't a charity. So who's paying the commission on a job likely to consume ages untold—the kid or you?”

lines.japanese: 「オメェ～よお？　アァ～？　しょっぺえこと、ゆーなっつってんだろ？」
lines.english: “Youuu... listen here... huh? I told you to quit talking such stingy little shit.”

lines.japanese: 女は俺の胸倉を掴んで、細く刈った眉毛を八の字にした。パルさんは背中にカラフルな彫り物をした大人たちがはびこる街の出身でもあった。
lines.english: The woman seized my lapels, her narrowly plucked brows bending into a mournful arch. Paru also hailed from a town overrun by grown men with colorful pictures across their backs.

lines.japanese: 「ばか、放せてめ、どっちがしょっぱいんだよ。んな言うなら、てめーでやれっつうの」
lines.english: “Idiot, let go. Who are you calling stingy? If it matters that much, do it yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「ハーッ！　てやんでィ、根無し草のプー太郎が、ええッ、一丁前のクチ利いてんじゃないよ！　あんたちっとも社会に貢献してねェんだ、たまにゃ慈善事業ぐれーしやがれってんだよコンチキショー」
lines.english: “Hah! You rootless unemployed bum! Don’t you get mouthy with me! You contribute nothing to society. Once in a while, you can damn well do a little charity!”

lines.japanese: 「してるっつーの。さっき、恵まれない青年に７円寄付したっつーの」
lines.english: “I do contribute. I donated seven yen to an underprivileged young man just now.”

lines.japanese: 「しゃらくせえよ」
lines.english: “Don’t get cute with me.”

lines.japanese: 腕力まかせに逃げだそうとしたら、喉首すれすれにアイスピックの先端を突きつけられた。
lines.english: When I tried to wrench free, she thrust the point of an ice pick within a hair of my throat.
“Wha—!”

lines.japanese: 「……待て。まず待て。早まるな」
lines.english: “...Wait. First, wait. Don't be hasty.”

lines.japanese: 「なあコラ、ちっとぐれータダ働きしたって死にゃあしねえだろ、坊主」
lines.english: “Listen, kid. A little unpaid labor won't kill you.”

lines.japanese: 「ばか死ぬんだよ。死ぬぐらい生活困ってんだよ。今日の晩メシもデパ地下試食めぐりだったんだよ」
lines.english: “Yes, it will. I’m poor enough to die. For dinner tonight, I made the rounds of the free samples in a department-store basement.”

lines.japanese: 「おーし、ねーちゃん決まった！　こいつがあんたのチャリ、探してくれるってさ！」
lines.english: “All right, miss, it's settled! This boy says he'll find your bike!”

lines.japanese: 「おい。おい待てコラ。『くれるってさ』じゃねーよ。なに勝手に決めてんだよ」
lines.english: “Hey. Hey, wait. Don't give me ‘he says.’ What are you doing deciding for me?”

lines.japanese: 「しかも特別サービスで金はいらねえってよ！」
lines.english: “And as a special service, he says you don't owe him a cent!”

lines.japanese: 「うるせーばか。もういい、おまえ喋んな。マジ喋んな」
lines.english: “Shut up, idiot. Enough. Stop talking. Seriously, don't talk.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、ほんとにいいんですかー」
lines.english: “Are you really sure that's all right?”

lines.japanese: 「いいわけねーだろ、おまえも。話の流れ読めよ」
lines.english: “Of course it isn’t. You too—read the room.”

lines.japanese: 「ピーピーうるさいガキだねえ、ったく、ケツの穴の小さいこと言ってんじゃないよ」
lines.english: “What a whiny little brat. Honestly, quit talking like such a tight-ass.”

lines.japanese: 「んだてめ、小さくて悪りぃのかよ」
lines.english: “What, is there something wrong with mine being tight?”

lines.japanese: 「小さいんですかー」
lines.english: “Is yours tight?”

lines.japanese: 「訊いてんじゃねーよ、おまえも。小さくねーっつの。なめんなよ、てめ。俺のはハンパねえっつーの。マジ度肝抜くっつーの。さながらブラックホールだかんな、見せんぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Don't ask! And it isn't tight. Don't underestimate me. Mine is unbelievable. It'll knock you senseless. It's practically a black hole. I'll show you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょーちょーおまえ、言わせといて勝手に引くな？」
lines.english: “Whoa, whoa. Don't make me say all that and then recoil on your own.”

lines.japanese: 「で？　ねーちゃん、パクられたチャリってどんなんだい」
lines.english: “So, miss, what did the stolen bicycle look like?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ……コラ待て女、なんで話が進むんだよ」
lines.english: “Hey... wait, woman. Why is the conversation advancing?”

lines.japanese: 「しゃーあんめえよ、あんたの肛門なんざ誰も興味ねえんだから」
lines.english: “Can't be helped. Nobody cares about your anus.”

lines.japanese: 「だから。なんでお題目が肛門と自転車の二択なんだよ。もっと他にあんだろ、コイバナとかナサバナとか」
lines.english: “That's my point. Why are the only two available topics my anus and a bicycle? Other subjects exist. Love stories. NASA stories.”

lines.japanese: 「赤い自転車です、前に籠代わりのポーチが付いてましてー」
lines.english: “It's a red bicycle, with a pouch mounted in front instead of a basket.”

lines.japanese: 「だから話進めんなって、おまえも」
lines.english: “I said don't advance the conversation. You too.”

lines.japanese: 「あとシートに背もたれが付いてますー」
lines.english: “And the seat has a backrest.”

lines.japanese: 「進めんなっつの。んな、聞いてねーんだよ」
lines.english: “Quit advancing it. I didn't ask.”

lines.japanese: 「え……いま、なんつった？　背もたれ？　チャリンコなのに？」
lines.english: “Wait... what did you say? A backrest? On a bicycle?”

lines.japanese: 「はいー、背もたれですー」
lines.english: “Yes. A backrest.”

lines.japanese: 小娘は両腕を前へ伸ばし、見えない何かへもたれるように背中を反らせた。チョッパーハンドルのアメリカンバイクにふんぞり返る不良中年みたいだ。
lines.english: The girl extended both arms and arched her back against something invisible. She looked like a middle-aged delinquent lounging astride a cruiser motorcycle with chopper handlebars.

lines.japanese: 「はあ……まあ、よく分かんねーけどさ。そんな高そうなチャリ、無用心にその辺置いとく方にも問題あんじゃねーの」
lines.english: “Huh... Well, I don't really understand it, but don't you share some blame for carelessly leaving such an expensive-sounding bicycle around?”

lines.japanese: 「きっとあんたみたいのが、痴漢でしょっぴかれても逆ギレして『そんな破廉恥な格好してる方が悪い』とか言うんだろうねえ」
lines.english: “I bet if you were arrested for groping, you'd fly into a rage and say, ‘She's the one at fault for dressing so shamelessly.’”

lines.japanese: 「言わねえよ」
lines.english: “I wouldn't say that.”

lines.japanese: 「痴漢でしょっぴかれるは否定しないんですか」
lines.english: “You don't deny the part where you get arrested for groping?”

lines.japanese: 俺はツッコミを入れる代わりに小娘の顔を下から睨みあげた（しかしやつは怯まない。たくましくなったもんだ）。
lines.english: Instead of firing back, I glared up into the girl's face from below. She didn't flinch. How strong she had grown.

lines.japanese: 「でも、アレだねえ、そんな分かりやすい自転車ならすぐ見つけられンじゃないかねえ」
lines.english: “Still, a bicycle that distinctive ought to be easy to find, shouldn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「はいー、かなり目立つとは思うんです」
lines.english: “Yes. I think it stands out considerably.”

lines.japanese: 「ですから、仕事の道すがらなどにたまたまそれっぽい自転車を見かけたらで結構です。たまたま見かけたら、ご一報いただけますでしょうか」
lines.english: “So it would be enough if you happened to see something like it in the course of your work. If you happen across it, could you let me know?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 俺を見上げる小娘の表情は、意外と真剣モードだった。
lines.english: The girl's face as she looked up at me had turned unexpectedly serious.

lines.japanese: 俺が黙って眉をひそめていると、パルさんがおっかねえ顔をしてステンレスの調理台をどんと叩いた。
lines.english: I frowned in silence. Paru put on a terrifying scowl and slammed the stainless-steel worktop.

lines.japanese: 「あァ、まァ……たまたま見かけたらな。まァ、そんぐらいの協力はするけど」
lines.english: “Uh, sure... if I happen to see it. I can do that much.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、でもおまえ、アレだぞマジで。悪いけど、積極的に探してやったりは出来ねーかんな」
lines.english: “But I'm serious. Sorry, but I can't go out and actively search for it.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、もちろんですー。たしかにおっしゃる通り、現状での捜索願いはセアカゴケグモを掴むような話ですよねー」
lines.english: “Yes, of course. As you said, asking for a search under present conditions would be like trying to grab a redback spider.”

lines.japanese: 小娘は照れたように笑った。でも、そんなことは俺に言われるまでもなく、ここに来る前から本人がいちばんよく分かってたはずだ。分かってて来たはずだ。
lines.english: The girl smiled in embarrassment. But she must have known that better than anyone before she ever came here. She had come anyway.

lines.japanese: 図々しさを演じきれない子供。ふん。思わずふらりと情に流されそうになったけど、いやいや、だって無理なもんは無理だ。
lines.english: A child who couldn’t quite sustain the performance of shamelessness. Hmph. For a moment, sympathy nearly swept me along, but no. The impossible remained impossible.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、いちお気には留めとくけど。でもおまえ、あんま期待はすんじゃねーぞ。たぶん見つかんないから」
lines.english: “I’ll keep it in mind, at least. But don’t get your hopes up. It probably won’t turn up.”

lines.japanese: 俺ははっきりと言っておいた。べつに女子供を泣かせる趣味はない。でも世の中には、突きはなす優しさだってあると思うんだ。
lines.english: I made that perfectly clear. It wasn’t as though I enjoyed making women and children cry. But sometimes the kind thing was to push someone away.

lines.japanese: それに──
lines.english: Besides—

lines.japanese: 「ドラ！　あんた、それを言っちゃあおしめえだよ」
lines.english: “Dora! You say that and it’s all over.”

lines.japanese: ──どうせパルさんがフォローしてくれることは分かってる。
lines.english: —Besides, I knew Paru would soften the blow for me.

lines.japanese: 「ねーちゃん、そしたらよ、また気が向いたらうち寄っとくれ。ドラ、あんたは赤い背もたれ付きの自転車を見かけたらあたしに報告だ。いいね？」
lines.english: “Miss, come by again whenever you feel like it. Dora, if you see a red bicycle with a backrest, you report it to me. Understood?”

lines.japanese: 「へーへー」
lines.english: “Sure, sure.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとうございます。よろしくお願いします」
lines.english: “Thank you very much. I appreciate your help.”

lines.japanese: 小娘はバカ丁寧に深々と頭を下げた。俺とパル姐さんに二回ずつ。
lines.english: The girl bowed with absurd depth and formality—twice apiece to Paru and me.

lines.japanese: 「しっかしまァ、ほんとに見つかってほしいやなあ」
lines.english: “Still, I really hope it turns up.”

lines.japanese: 「まぁアレだ。見つかんなかったらモンキ行けモンキ。マジ、爆安の殿堂だからモンキ」
lines.english: “Well, if it doesn’t turn up, go to Monki. Seriously—Monki Hote, the palace of blowout bargains.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい、そうですね。せっかく教えていただきましたから、もし新車を買うことがあればモンキホウーテに行ってまいります」
lines.english: “Ah, yes. Since you were kind enough to tell me, if I buy a new bicycle, I'll visit Monki Hoote.”

lines.japanese: 「だな、そうしろ。安いからモンキホーテ。マジ、爆安の殿堂だから。あと『モンキホーテ』な。『ウ』はいらないから」
lines.english: “Yeah, do that. Monki Hote is cheap. Seriously—the palace of blowout bargains. And it’s *Monki Hote*. No extra ‘o.’”

lines.japanese: 「ねーちゃん、場所分かんの？」
lines.english: “Miss, do you know where it is?”

lines.japanese: 「えーはいモンキホウーテですよねー、花水木通りの奥の方でしたっけー」
lines.english: “Yes, Monki Hoote, right? Wasn't it toward the far end of Flowering Dogwood Street?”

lines.japanese: 「ああドラ、地図でも書いたげな」
lines.english: “Dora, draw her a map.”

lines.japanese: パルさんがカウンターの内側にあったメモ用紙を一枚破って、ペンと一緒に差しだしてきた。
lines.english: Paru tore one sheet from the memo pad behind the counter and offered it with a pen.

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なんでだよ、めんどくせーな」
lines.english: “Huh? Why? What a pain.”

lines.japanese: しかし顔面に押しつけられて邪魔だったので、受けとらざるを得なかった。
lines.english: But she shoved the paper and pen into my face, so I had no choice but to take them.

lines.japanese: 猫の額みたいなパルクレープ号のボンネットを下敷きにして、紙の真ん中に細長い四角を描きなぐる。
lines.english: Using the matchbox hood of the Paru Crêpes van as a writing board, I scrawled a long, narrow rectangle in the center of the paper.

lines.japanese: 「だから駅がここじゃん、ここ。これ柳木原駅な。あとおまえ『ウ』はいらないから」
lines.english: “So the station is here. Here. This is Yanagihara Station. And you still don't need the extra ‘o.’”

lines.japanese: 「はー、なんと言うか、力強いパッションを感じさせる大胆な地図ですね」
lines.english: “My. What a bold map. I can feel the tremendous passion behind it.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえな、いいんだよ。芸術は爆発なんだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up, it's fine. Art is an explosion.”

lines.japanese: 覗きこんでくる四つの目を鬱陶しく思いながら、俺は適当にペンを走らせる。
lines.english: Annoyed by the four eyes peering over my work, I let the pen wander at random.

lines.japanese: 「で、駅からこう……これが花水木通りで、こっちがグローヴ通り、あとなんかこう色々あんじゃん」
lines.english: “From the station you go like this... This is Flowering Dogwood Street, this is Grove Street, and then there's, you know, various other stuff.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだか爆発ってわりにゃあ線がよれてるねえ。花水木通り、先細りしてんじゃないか」
lines.english: “For an explosion, those lines sure wobble. Flowering Dogwood Street is tapering away to nothing.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえな、いいんだよ。俺の地図はモルワイデ図法なんだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up, it's fine. My map uses the Mollweide projection.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、なんですか、その『文』って。この辺りに学校なんてありましたっけ？」
lines.english: “What's that little school symbol? Was there a school around here?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ、あんじゃん三丁目に。私立ぬるぬる女学院」
lines.english: “Sure. Slippery Girls' Academy in the third district.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ言っとくけど、いくら名前が学校っぽくてもイメクラの地図記号は『文』じゃないからな」
lines.english: “Listen, however much the name sounds like a school, an erotic role-play club does not get a school symbol on the map.”

lines.japanese: 「あのー、すいません、その前にまず現在地はどこですか」
lines.english: “Um, excuse me. Before any of that, where are we now?”

lines.japanese: 「現在地。あー、現在地な、現在地は……うん。ねえな」
lines.english: “Our present location. Right. Our present location is... Hmm. Doesn't exist.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、『ねえな』じゃねえだろ。じゃあ、あたしらがいまいるここはなんだ。四次元か」
lines.english: “You don't get to say ‘doesn't exist.’ Then what is this place we're standing in? The fourth dimension?”

lines.japanese: 「ばかおまえ、違げんだよ。実はコレ地図とかじゃねんだよ。内緒だけど実はコレ未来予想図なんだよ。実は４５年後に、この辺一帯はダムに沈んで地図から消えるんだよ」
lines.english: “Idiot, you don’t get it. This isn’t an ordinary map. Keep it secret, but it’s a future map. Forty-five years from now, this whole area will sink beneath a dam and disappear from the map.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、４５年後も私立ぬるぬる女学院は健在ですか」
lines.english: “Oh. So Slippery Girls' Academy will still be thriving forty-five years from now.”

lines.japanese: 「つーか、むしろ国立になってんな」
lines.english: “If anything, it's gone national.”

lines.japanese: 「ダムの底で？」
lines.english: “At the bottom of a reservoir?”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえな、いいんだよ。ぬる女は２１世紀に甦った竜宮城なんだよ。で、ほら、ここがモンキホーテだ。な、ほら、コレおまえにやるから大事にしまっとけ」
lines.english: “Shut up, it's fine. Slippery Girls' Academy is the Dragon Palace reborn in the twenty-first century. And look, here's Monki Hote. There. I'm giving you this, so treasure it.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい、ありがとうございます。向こう４５年はこれを頼りにモンキホウーテへ参ります」
lines.english: “Ah, yes. Thank you. For the next forty-five years, I shall rely upon it whenever traveling to Monki Hoote.”

lines.japanese: 「おう、がんばれよ。あと４５年経っても『ウ』は付かないから」
lines.english: “Yeah, good luck. And even forty-five years from now, there still won't be an extra ‘o.’”

lines.japanese: 小娘は受けとった未来予想図を畳みながら、へこりと頭を下げた。
lines.english: The girl folded up the future map I had given her and bobbed her head.

lines.japanese: そして制服のポケットにしまうと、それではお世話様でしたと言ってまた頭を下げる。よく頭を下げるやつだ。今日何度目かはもう忘れた。
lines.english: She tucked it into her uniform pocket, thanked us for our help, and bowed yet again. She really did bow a lot. I’d lost count of how many times she had done it today.

lines.japanese: これでようやく解散かと思ったら、クレープ屋がやつを呼びとめた。
lines.english: I thought that was finally the end of it, but the crêpe seller called her back.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと待った、ねーちゃん。あんたさ、良かったらケータイの番号教えとくれよ。なんか進展あったら連絡したげるからさ」
lines.english: “Hold on, miss. If you don't mind, give me your cell number. I'll let you know if anything develops.”
“Pardon...?”

lines.japanese: つくづく世話好きなおばはんだ。小娘の呆けたアホ面が、ゆっくり花咲くように輝いた。
lines.english: That meddlesome old woman really couldn’t help herself. The girl’s blank, foolish face slowly brightened like a flower opening.

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい！　ありがとうございます！　えとあの、携帯電話は持ってないんですけど──」
lines.english: “Ah, yes! Thank you! Um, well, I don't have a cell phone—”

lines.japanese: やつは言いながら慌ててバッグに手を突っこんだが、すぐにぴたりと動きを止めて頭を上げた。
lines.english: As she spoke, she thrust a hand into her bag. Then she stopped dead and looked up.

lines.japanese: 「──持ってないんですよ」
lines.english: “—I don't have one, you see.”

lines.japanese: その妙なリアクションが引っかかったパルさんは、俺の耳に顔を近づけて聞こえよがしな掠れ声を出す。
lines.english: The peculiar reaction caught Paru’s attention. She leaned toward my ear and stage-whispered loudly enough to be heard.

lines.japanese: 「あら？　ひょっとしてあたし、警戒されてる？」
lines.english: “Oh? Could it be she doesn't trust me?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、するだろフツー。鏡見ろよ」
lines.english: “Obviously she doesn't. Look in a mirror.”

lines.japanese: 「あああ、いえ違います違います。本当です、本当に携帯電話なんて持ってないんです。ほら！　ほらほら！　ほらっ！」
lines.english: “Ohhh, no, no! That's not it. It's true. I truly don't own a cell phone. Look! Look, look! Look!”

lines.japanese: 小娘、必死にカバンの口を広げ、乙女のひみつを大公開。その中はやけに教科書やノートが少なくて意外にがらがらだった。ともかくパルさんは安心したみたいだった。
lines.english: The girl desperately stretched open her bag and unveiled every maidenly secret. Surprisingly few textbooks or notebooks occupied the almost empty interior. In any event, Paru seemed reassured.

lines.japanese: 「なんだい、一瞬おねーさん嫌われたのかと思ったよ。いやほら、いまどきの子はみんなケータイ持ってるだろ。あんたは真面目な子だね」
lines.english: “Oh, for a moment I thought the young lady disliked me. It's only that every kid has a cell phone these days. You must be a serious girl.”

lines.japanese: 「どういう論理だよ。つか、ケータイなら俺も持ってねーんだけど」
lines.english: “What kind of logic is that? I don't own a cell phone either.”

lines.japanese: 「あんたは金がないだけだろ」
lines.english: “You’re just broke.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで知ってんだよ」
lines.english: “How do you know?”

lines.japanese: ──まあ、本当はそれだけが理由じゃないんだけど、他人に説明するようなことではないから金のせいにしておいた。
lines.english: —Though money wasn't truly the only reason. It wasn't something I needed to explain to other people, so I let money shoulder the blame.

lines.japanese: 俺もいろいろ大変なんだよ。
lines.english: I had plenty to deal with too, you know.

lines.japanese: 「ちなみに私の場合はー、友達いないので携帯電話を持つ必要性がないんですー」
lines.english: “In my case, incidentally, I have no friends, so I have no need for a cell phone.”

lines.japanese: 「へー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそう」
lines.english: “Right.”

lines.japanese: やつが何気なく漏らした言葉に対し、俺とパル姐さんは淡白に返答した。とくにピックアップするほど面白い冗談ではなかった。そんな話なら俺たちは聞きあきてる。
lines.english: She let the words drop casually, and Paru and I answered with equal indifference. It wasn’t a joke worth singling out. We’d heard that story too many times.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ家デン聞いてもいいかい」
lines.english: “Could I have your home number, then?”

lines.japanese: やけに明るく優しい声でパルさんが尋ねた。
lines.english: Paru asked in an unusually bright and gentle voice.

lines.japanese: 「あ、自宅ですか、はい」
lines.english: “Oh, my home? Yes.”

lines.japanese: 小娘はにっこり頷きながら、カウンターに置きはなしていたあのペンを取った。すらすらと新しいメモ用紙に１０桁の数字をつづる。
lines.english: The girl smiled, nodded, and picked up the pen abandoned on the counter. In one flowing movement she wrote ten digits across a fresh memo sheet.

lines.japanese: 典型的な乙女の丸文字。馴染みぶかい局番。そしてその上に漢字をふたつ並べる──鳳鳴。
lines.english: Typical girlish bubble letters. A familiar area code. Then, above them, two written characters crowded together with no break: *Phoenixsong*.

lines.japanese: 「ほうめい……？」
lines.english: “Phoenix Song...?”

lines.japanese: 「なんだィこれ。あんたっとこ中華料理屋？」
lines.english: “What's this? Does your family run a Chinese restaurant?”

lines.japanese: 「あーいえ、名前ですねー私の」
lines.english: “Oh, no. That is my name.”

lines.japanese: 小娘は人差し指の上でペンをくるっと一回転させてから、そいつを頭上に掲げて握りなおし、ふたつの文字のあいだに力強く中黒を打った──鳳・鳴。
lines.english: The girl spun the pen once around her index finger, raised it above her head, changed her grip, and drove a forceful dot between the two characters, forcing the proper name apart: *Otori · Naru*.

lines.japanese: 「えー、わたくし『おおとり・なる』と申しますー」
lines.english: “My name is Naru Otori.”

lines.japanese: その名を耳にしたとき、俺の体がぴくりと自動的に反応した。
lines.english: At the sound of the name, my body gave an involuntary twitch.

lines.japanese: 「……おおとり？」
lines.english: “...Otori?”

lines.japanese: 「あらあら、可愛いナリしてまた仰々しい名前なんだね、どうも」
lines.english: “My, my. Such a grand name for such a cute little thing.”

lines.japanese: 「あはー、親と名前は選べませんしー」
lines.english: “Ha ha. One cannot choose one's parents or one's name.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、おめでたそうないい名前じゃないか。ああそうだ、申しおくれちゃったね。あたしはパル。こっちはドラ」
lines.english: “No, no. It's a fine, auspicious name. Ah, I forgot to introduce us. I'm Paru. This is Dora.”

lines.japanese: 「芸名ですかー？」
lines.english: “Are those stage names?”

lines.japanese: 「なんのだよ」
lines.english: “Stage names for what?”

lines.japanese: 「つーか、はい、質問」
lines.english: “More importantly: question.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、なんでしょう」
lines.english: “Yes? What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、ひょっとしたら。ひょっとしたらだけどな」
lines.english: “I mean, maybe. Just maybe, though.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえン家まさか、やたら背ェ高くて、やたらイケメンで、やたら態度のでかい男とかいねーよな？」
lines.english: “There isn't, by any chance, some man in your family who's absurdly tall, absurdly handsome, and absurdly full of himself?”
“Pardon?”

lines.japanese: 「あーいや、悪りい悪りい、何でもない。そうだよな、いるわきゃねーよな。まさかな、んな偶然な」
lines.english: “Ah, no, sorry, sorry. Nothing. Of course there isn't. What are the odds of a coincidence like that?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、なんだ。ちょっとさ、たまたまおまえと同じ苗字のやつ知ってたからさ」
lines.english: “No, it's just... I happen to know this guy with the same last name as you.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、ドラさんは兄をご存知なんですか？」
lines.english: “Oh. Dora, do you know my older brother?”

lines.japanese: 俺は一瞬の硬直ののち、静かに首を振った。
lines.english: I froze for a second, then quietly shook my head.

lines.japanese: 「いや……全然……」
lines.english: “No... not at all...”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだい、変な子だねえ」
lines.english: “What a strange boy.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、いや、ひょっとしたら。ひょっとしたらなんだけどさ……」
lines.english: “Uh, no. Maybe. Just maybe, though...”

lines.japanese: 「そいつの名前、カケルとか言わねーよな？」
lines.english: “His name isn't Kakeru, is it?”

lines.japanese: 「ああー、ドラさんは兄のお友達のひとだったんですかー」
lines.english: “Ohhh. Dora, are you one of my brother's friends?”

lines.japanese: 「おう、そうだったんかい。こりゃ大した偶然だ」
lines.english: “Well, how about that? What a coincidence.”

lines.japanese: 俺は数瞬の硬直ののち、静かに首を振った。
lines.english: I froze for several seconds, then quietly shook my head.

lines.japanese: 「いや、違くて……友達とかじゃなくて……」
lines.english: “No. That's not... We aren't friends...”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、えーと、いつも兄がお世話になっております」
lines.english: “I see. Well, thank you for always taking care of my brother.”

lines.japanese: 「ばっ……やめろてめ、アタマ下げんな。マジまったく世話とかしてねーから。つーかおまえ、俺に会ったこととか兄貴に言わなくていいからな」
lines.english: “Wha—stop that. Don't bow. I have never taken care of him in any way. And you don't need to tell your brother you met me, understood?”

lines.japanese: 「つーか言うなよ。言ったら泣かすかんな。ブラックホールとか見せっかんな至近距離で」
lines.english: “Actually, don't tell him. If you do, I'll make you cry. I'll show you the black hole from point-blank range.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、えーと、よく分からないですけどー、とりあえず今後とも兄をよろしくお願いいたします」
lines.english: “I don't quite understand, but, um... please continue to treat my brother well.”
“Impossible.”

lines.japanese: そんじゃ、と強引にシメて俺はパル姐さんのクレープ屋をあとにした。つーか逃げた。
lines.english: I forced the conversation to a close with a quick “Later” and left Paru’s crêpe shop. More accurately, I fled.

lines.japanese: 幸運にもここ一ヵ月ぐらいあの男に遭遇しないでいられたのに、その家族とかかわりを持つなんて。そんなの、自分からやつを呼びよせるようなものだ。
lines.english: I’d been lucky enough to avoid that man for nearly a month, and now I’d gone and gotten involved with his family. I might as well have summoned him myself.

lines.japanese: 俺は何も聞かなかったことにして、ひたすら速いペースで道を急ぐ。
lines.english: I pretended I hadn’t heard any of it and hurried away as fast as I could.

lines.japanese: それでも、放置自転車がずらりと並ぶ歩道に差しかかればつい足取りもゆっくりになってしまうあたり、俺は案外お人好しなんだと思う。
lines.english: Even so, when I reached a sidewalk lined with abandoned bicycles, I found myself slowing down. Apparently I was more of a soft touch than I’d thought.

lines.japanese: 前にポーチが付いた……背もたれ付きの……真っ赤なチャリ……。
lines.english: A pouch in front... a backrest... a bright red bike...

lines.japanese: だけどやっぱり、そいつはそう簡単に見つかったりしなかった。
lines.english: But of course it wasn’t that easy to find.
